title: Output Contracts: JSON or It Didn't Happen
objective: After this lesson you will be able to specify machine-readable outputs (JSON schemas, enums, delimiters), parse model output defensively (fences, prose, repair), and choose the strictness level each consumer needs.
why: Model output feeds code: routers switch on categories, UIs render fields, databases store rows. Prose answers break pipelines — 'Category: billing (I think?)' crashes parsers. Contracts convert creativity into interfaces: demand exact shapes, parse defensively anyway, and match strictness to the consumer (code needs schemas, humans need readability).

blocks.text: Specify **keys, types, enums, and nothing-else clauses**: `Output JSON exactly {"category": one of [billing, shipping, returns], "confidence": 0-1}. No prose, no markdown, no extra keys.` Each clause deletes a failure: enums kill invented labels, types kill 'high' instead of 0.9, nothing-else kills chatty prefixes. Vague shape requests ('respond in JSON') still admit prose-wrapped JSON — exactness is the whole game.

blocks.code:
OUTPUT CONTRACT:
Respond with EXACTLY this JSON object, no surrounding text:
{"category": "billing" | "shipping" | "returns",
 "confidence": <number 0..1>,
 "reason": "<12 words max>"}
Forbidden: markdown fences, explanations, extra keys, null confidence.
blocks.caption: Contract anatomy: exact keys, enums, ranges, and explicit forbiddens

blocks.text: Contracts reduce violations; they don't eliminate them. The defensive parser tries, in order: direct `JSON.parse`; extract the first `{…}`/`[…]` span; strip markdown fences; repair trailing commas; and only then **quarantine with the raw text preserved** (the data-pipeline discipline from OpenDataLoader, applied to model output). Never `eval`, never silent defaults — a defaulted category is a lie with good formatting.

blocks.caption: Parse in layers, quarantine with evidence — silent defaults forbidden

blocks.text: Match strictness to what reads the output. **Code paths** (routers, DB writes): strictest — enums, types, nothing-else, plus schema validation post-parse (Ch.3 of OpenDataLoader thinking). **Human review queues**: medium — structured but readable (bullets, short fields). **Exploratory/chat**: loose — readability first. Escalating strictness everywhere wastes effort and degrades quality; relaxing it on code paths breaks production.

blocks.title: Break the parser, then fix the contract
blocks.note: Run it: expect PARSED ×3 (direct, fenced, embedded) then QUARANTINED for the prose one — which no contract wording can fully prevent, hence quarantine-with-evidence as the final layer.

items: Contracts: exact keys, enums, types, nothing-else clauses — vagueness here breaks pipelines
Parse in layers (direct → fence → span → quarantine); never eval, never silent defaults
Strictness follows the consumer: code strictest, review medium, chat loose

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice parser on the four cases and record which layer catches each. (b) Add a fifth case with a trailing comma ('{"a": 1,}') — observe quarantine, then add a repair layer (trailing-comma strip) and re-run. (c) Write the output contract for the returns decision (approved bool, reason ≤12 words, next_step enum) with two forbiddens.
hints: Layer mapping: direct → case 1; fence-strip → case 2; span-extract → case 3; quarantine → case 4. Say it explicitly per case.
Repair layer: .replace(/,(\s*[}\]])/g, '$1') before parsing — insert as a new attempt between span and quarantine. Re-run: case 5 now PARSED.
Contract needs: exact keys with types, enum for next_step ([label, escalate, refund]), ≤12-word reason, forbiddens (no prose, no extra keys).
exercise.why: Layered parsing plus contract authoring is the complete output discipline: demand exactly, accept defensively, quarantine honestly. The trailing-comma repair shows the layer list is extensible by evidence, not fixed.

quiz.q: 'Respond in JSON' still yields prose-wrapped JSON. Missing contract clauses?
options: Exact keys + enums + nothing-else/forbidden clauses (no prose, no fences, no extra keys)
quiz.explain: Shape requests without exactness admit decorated JSON. Enums kill invented labels, nothing-else kills chatty wrappers.

quiz.q: Parser should handle unparseable output by…
options: Defaulting to the most common category
Quarantining with raw text preserved — silent defaults are lies with formatting
quiz.explain: Defaults corrupt downstream silently; eval executes attacker-influenced text. Quarantine preserves evidence for tuning and audit.

quiz.q: Strict JSON schemas for exploratory chat output. Verdict?
options: Mismatched strictness: code paths need schemas, chat needs readability — escalating everywhere wastes effort and quality
quiz.explain: Strictness follows the consumer. Uniform strictness taxes quality where humans read and under-protects where code parses — match, don't maximize.

summary: Demand exact shapes, parse in defensive layers, quarantine honestly, and calibrate strictness to the consumer. Contracts turn creativity into interfaces.
next: Shapes secured — now steer behavior with examples: selection, order, and the surprising power of negatives. Next: few-shot mastery.
